eyebrow: Data can change mid-query. Structure can too.
code:
-- S, X, U, intent locks -- all protect DATA
-- A table's SCHEMA (columns, types, constraints)
-- needs its OWN lock category.
caption: A column vanishing mid-query is a different hazard entirely.

eyebrow: Sch-S: taken on nearly every ordinary query
code:
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ProductID = 680;
-- Takes a Sch-S lock for the duration of the statement.
caption: Guarantees the table's structure can't change mid-query.

eyebrow: Sch-M: taken during DDL, incompatible with everything
caption: A structural change can't happen while any query runs against it.

code:
-- Session B's SELECT running first (holds Sch-S)
--   -> Session A's ALTER TABLE (needs Sch-M) WAITS
-- Session A's ALTER TABLE running first (holds Sch-M)
--   -> Session B's SELECT (needs Sch-S) WAITS
caption: Why ALTER TABLE on a busy table can seem to "just hang."
